subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Functional pancreatic NETs and primary aldosteronism

steps.tx: **Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors** (pNETs, growths from the hormone-making cells of the pancreas) are mostly silent. Only about 20 percent of them release enough hormone to cause symptoms. Among the functional types, **insulinoma** is the most common, followed by **glucagonoma** and **gastrinoma**. Each secreting tumor produces its own recognizable syndrome, so the pattern of symptoms points toward the hormone responsible.
steps.say: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, usually shortened to pNETs, grow from the hormone-making cells of the pancreas. Most of them are silent. Only about 20 percent release enough hormone to cause symptoms. Among the functional types, insulinoma is the most common, with glucagonoma and gastrinoma following behind. Each tumor produces its own recognizable syndrome, so the pattern of symptoms points toward the hormone responsible.

rows: Skin rash, weight loss, high blood sugar
More than 50 percent spread at diagnosis

steps.tx: **Insulinoma** reveals itself through the **Whipple triad** (three findings that together establish low blood sugar: symptoms, a low measured glucose, and relief once glucose rises). Observed fasting that shows insulin over 3 microunits per milliliter, often over 6, while glucose sits below 40 to 45 milligrams per deciliter confirms the diagnosis. Proinsulin and **C-peptide** (a fragment released alongside the body's own insulin) rise with it. Most insulinomas measure under 2 cm, so **endoscopic ultrasound** (EUS) is the best local test.
steps.say: Insulinoma is recognized through the Whipple triad. That triad has three parts: symptoms of low blood sugar, a low glucose reading taken accurately, and relief of symptoms once glucose rises. Observed fasting that shows insulin over 3 microunits per milliliter, often over 6, while glucose sits below 40 to 45 milligrams per deciliter confirms the diagnosis. Proinsulin and C-peptide, a fragment released alongside insulin, rise with it. Most insulinomas measure under 2 centimeters, so endoscopic ultrasound is the best local test.

steps.tx: **Gastrinoma** drives **Zollinger-Ellison syndrome** (ZES, excess stomach acid caused by too much gastrin, the hormone that tells acid-making cells to work). The result is ulcers and diarrhea. A fasting gastrin above 600 picograms per milliliter is typical, and virtually all patients exceed 100. A gastrin level of 1,000 or more, paired with a gastric pH of 2 or less, secures the diagnosis. **Proton pump inhibitors** (PPIs, acid-suppressing drugs) can raise gastrin and mislead the test.
steps.say: Gastrinoma drives Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, which means excess stomach acid caused by too much gastrin, the hormone that tells acid-making cells to work. The result is ulcers and diarrhea. A fasting gastrin above 600 picograms per milliliter is typical, and virtually all patients exceed 100. A gastrin level of 1,000 or more, paired with a gastric pH of 2 or less, secures the diagnosis. Proton pump inhibitors, which are acid-suppressing drugs, can raise gastrin and mislead the test.

rows: 1,000 pg/mL or more, pH 2 or less
Duodenum is the most common site

steps.tx: **Glucagonoma** most often shows **necrolytic migratory erythema** (a painful rash in skin folds such as the groin that waxes and wanes), with glucose intolerance and weight loss. Plasma glucagon generally above 1,000 picograms per milliliter supports the diagnosis. **VIPoma**, a tumor secreting vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), causes watery diarrhea, low potassium, and low stomach acid (achlorhydria). That combination is called Verner-Morrison syndrome.
steps.say: Patients with glucagonoma usually develop necrolytic migratory erythema, a painful rash in skin folds such as the groin that waxes and wanes. Glucose intolerance and weight loss usually come with it. Plasma glucagon generally above 1,000 picograms per milliliter supports the diagnosis. VIPoma is a tumor that secretes vasoactive intestinal peptide, causing watery diarrhea, low potassium, and low stomach acid. That combination is called Verner-Morrison syndrome.

left.title: Glucagonoma
points: Necrolytic migratory erythema in skin folds

right.title: VIPoma
points: Watery diarrhea, often over 20 stools a day
Most arise in the pancreas in adults

steps.tx: Up to 25 percent of people with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome also have **multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1** (MEN 1, an inherited syndrome of tumors in several glands). Gastrinomas in this setting tend to be small and multiple. Pancreatic tumors in MEN 1 often grow slowly, yet partial pancreatectomy can leave new tumors in the remaining gland, so surgeons weigh each operation carefully.
steps.say: As many as one in four people with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome also carry multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1. Clinicians abbreviate that as MEN 1, an inherited syndrome producing tumors in several glands. Gastrinomas in MEN 1 tend to be small and multiple. Pancreatic tumors there often grow slowly. Partial removal of the pancreas may leave new tumors behind, so surgeons weigh each operation carefully.

steps.tx: Overall, **most pNETs are malignant**, and insulinoma is the exception, benign in 95 percent of patients. **Gastrinoma** is the functional type with the clearest high malignant share: more than 60 percent are judged malignant. A recent review adds that more than half of VIPomas have spread at diagnosis, that 50 to 80 percent of glucagonomas have spread by then, and that more than 60 percent of somatostatinomas are malignant.

left.title: Gastrinoma
points: Malignant by local invasion or spread
Regional lymph node removal is important

right.title: Insulinoma
points: No lymph node dissection if nonmetastatic

steps.tx: **Primary aldosteronism** means the adrenal glands make aldosterone on their own, keeping renin suppressed. It appears in 5 to 12 percent of people with hypertension in systematic screening. The usual screen is the **aldosterone-to-renin ratio** (ARR, a comparison of two blood hormones) taken after stopping **spironolactone** for 4 to 6 weeks. A ratio above 20 becomes suggestive when renin is low or suppressed and aldosterone climbs past 12 ng/dL.
steps.say: Primary aldosteronism means the adrenal glands make aldosterone on their own, keeping renin suppressed. It appears in 5 to 12 percent of people with hypertension in systematic screening. The usual screen is the aldosterone-to-renin ratio, a comparison of two blood hormones, taken after stopping spironolactone for 4 to 6 weeks. A ratio above 20 becomes suggestive when renin is low or suppressed and aldosterone climbs past 12 ng/dL.

rows: Fine-cut CT of the adrenal glands
Often under 1 cm; CT can miss lesions under 5 mm

steps.tx: **Adrenal venous sampling** (AVS, catheters in each adrenal vein) compares aldosterone between the two sides, and cortisol confirms catheter placement. Patients under 35 with a unilateral lesion and no suspicion of a familial form can go straight to surgery. Patients over 35, or those with no obvious lesion on CT, need AVS first. A **saline infusion test** (2 liters over 4 hours) checks if aldosterone stays above 170 pmol/L while seated. A fine-cut CT shows adrenal anatomy and any unilateral adenoma, but **endocrine-inactive adenomas** are the most common adrenal mass.
steps.say: Adrenal venous sampling, or AVS, places catheters in each adrenal vein. It compares aldosterone levels between the two sides, and cortisol confirms the catheter placement. Patients under 35 with a unilateral lesion and no suspicion of a familial form can go straight to surgery. Patients over 35, or those with no obvious lesion on CT, need AVS first. A saline infusion test, with 2 liters given over 4 hours, checks if aldosterone stays above 170 picomoles per liter while seated. A fine-cut CT shows adrenal anatomy and any unilateral adenoma, but endocrine-inactive adenomas are the most common adrenal mass.

rows: Aldosterone above 170 pmol/L while seated means autonomous secretion
Shows adrenal anatomy and any unilateral adenoma; a nodule alone cannot show the source gland
Aldosterone-producing adenomas often under 1 cm; CT can miss lesions under 5 mm

Over 35, or no obvious lesion on CT

mustKnow.fact: In Zollinger-Ellison syndrome a fasting gastrin above 600 is typical and a gastrin of 1,000 or more with gastric pH of 2 or less secures the diagnosis.
Proton pump inhibitors can raise gastrin and mislead the diagnosis of gastrinoma.
Up to 25 percent of Zollinger-Ellison patients have multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, and MEN 1 gastrinomas are small and multiple.
Glucagonoma presents with necrolytic migratory erythema and plasma glucagon is generally above 1,000 pg/mL.
VIPoma causes watery diarrhea, low potassium and low stomach acid, the Verner-Morrison syndrome.
Primary aldosteronism is found in 5 to 12 percent of hypertensive patients on systematic screening.
mustKnow.source: Harrison, Chapter 398 Disorders of the Adrenal Cortex

mustKnow.fact: An aldosterone to renin ratio above 20 with suppressed renin and aldosterone above 12 ng/dL is suggestive of autonomous aldosterone.
Spironolactone is stopped for 4 to 6 weeks before the aldosterone-to-renin ratio screen.
mustKnow.source: Harrison, Chapter 398 Disorders of the Adrenal Cortex

mustKnow.fact: A saline infusion test of 2 liters over 4 hours shows autonomous aldosterone when aldosterone stays above 170 pmol/L seated.
mustKnow.source: Harrison, Chapter 398 Disorders of the Adrenal Cortex

mustKnow.fact: Endocrine-inactive adenomas are the most common adrenal mass, at 40 to 70 percent of unilateral lesions.
mustKnow.source: Harrison, Chapter 398 Disorders of the Adrenal Cortex (Table 398-5)
